description: Empire component knowledge database. Add new components here; the app picks them up without code changes.

components.name: Arduino Uno
components.description: ATmega328P development board with 14 digital I/O pins (6 PWM), 6 analog inputs, USB and 5V/3.3V regulators.
components.working: The microcontroller runs your compiled sketch from flash. Digital pins read or drive 0/5V logic; analog pins sample 0-5V into 10-bit values (0-1023); PWM pins produce a 0-5V square wave with variable duty cycle to approximate analog output.
components.current: 20mA max per pin, ~40mA per pin absolute max, 500mA via USB

arduino_examples.title: Blink LED on D13
arduino_examples.wiring: None (on-board LED) or LED + 220ohm resistor from D13 to GND
arduino_examples.code:
void setup(){ pinMode(13,OUTPUT); }
void loop(){ digitalWrite(13,HIGH); delay(1000); digitalWrite(13,LOW); delay(1000); }

void loop(){ Serial.println(digitalRead(2)); delay(200); }

void loop(){ for(int i=0;i<=255;i++){ analogWrite(9,i); delay(10);} for(int i=255;i>=0;i--){ analogWrite(9,i); delay(10);} }

arduino_examples.wiring: Servo signal to D9, VCC to 5V, GND to GND

components.esp32_notes: ESP32 runs at 3.3V logic: do not feed 5V logic directly into ESP32 inputs without a divider. Many Arduino libraries port directly.
common_mistakes: Forgetting common ground between board and sensors
components.safety_notes: Keep circuits under 5V unless using the VIN regulator. Disconnect USB before rewiring.

components.name: Arduino Nano
components.description: Compact breadboard-friendly ATmega328P board with the same core capabilities as the Uno.
components.working: Same 8-bit AVR architecture as the Uno but in a small DIP-style footprint. 14 digital pins (6 PWM), 8 analog inputs (A0-A7), micro-USB programming.

components.esp32_notes: Same caution: 3.3V logic on ESP32. The Nano's 5V output will damage ESP32 inputs directly.
components.safety_notes: Check pin orientation before powering; the Nano is easy to insert backwards.

components.name: Arduino Mega
components.description: ATmega2560 board with 54 digital pins, 15 PWM, 16 analog inputs, 4 UARTs — for larger projects.
components.working: Same 5V logic family as the Uno with far more I/O and memory (256KB flash, 8KB SRAM). Good for multi-sensor projects and multiple serial devices.

components.esp32_notes: Mega is 5V; ESP32 is 3.3V. Use level shifters or dividers when mixing them.
components.safety_notes: Use an external 5V supply for high-current loads, never through the USB port.

components.name: ESP32
components.description: Dual-core 240MHz Wi-Fi + Bluetooth module widely used for IoT. 3.3V logic with many GPIOs, ADC, DAC, PWM, I2C, SPI, UART.
components.working: Two Tensilica Xtensa cores run FreeRTOS. It boots from flash (Arduino core or ESP-IDF), provides Wi-Fi/BLE networking, and drives peripherals through multiplexed GPIO pins.
components.voltage: 3.3V logic, 3.3-5V USB power, up to 3.6V absolute max on inputs
components.current: ~12mA per GPIO (avoid sinking/sourcing large loads), total budget depends on regulator

arduino_examples.title: Blink onboard LED

Web server toggle LED
Read DHT22
arduino_examples.code:
#include <DHT.h>
DHT d(4,DHT22); void setup(){ Serial.begin(115200); d.begin(); } void loop(){ Serial.print(d.readTemperature()); Serial.print(','); Serial.println(d.readHumidity()); delay(2000); }

components.esp32_notes: ESP32 GPIOs are 3.3V and generally not 5V tolerant. ADC reads are nonlinear near extremes. Some pins (GPIO12, GPIO15) have boot-strapping functions — avoid them for critical output.
components.safety_notes: Never exceed 3.6V on any GPIO. Power motors/servos from a separate supply sharing common ground.

components.name: LED
components.description: Light-emitting diode. Polarized component that conducts current in one direction and emits light when forward-biased. Always use a current-limiting resistor.
components.working: An LED drops a forward voltage (Vf, typ. ~2V red / ~3.2V blue-white) across its junction. The resistor sets current: R = (V_supply - Vf) / I_desired. Typical target 10-20mA.

pins.name: Anode (+)
pins.function: Long leg, connects to supply via resistor

components.esp32_notes: Same resistor math; on ESP32 use 3.3V as supply, so R = (3.3 - Vf)/0.02 — a 100-220ohm resistor works for standard LEDs.
common_mistakes: Insufficient GPIO drive for high-power LEDs
components.safety_notes: High-power LEDs need drivers/transistors and heatsinks — never drive them from a GPIO directly.

components.name: Resistor
components.description: Passive two-terminal component that limits current and divides voltage. Value read from color bands or measured with a multimeter.
components.working: Obey's Ohm's law: V = I * R. Series resistors limit current to LEDs; voltage dividers scale signals; pull-ups/pull-downs define idle logic levels.
components.current: Limited by power rating: P = V*I, keep under 0.25W for 1/4W parts

components.esp32_notes: On 3.3V systems recalculate dividers so the ADC input stays below 3.3V.
common_mistakes: Using too-large values causing weak drive
components.safety_notes: A 1/4W resistor can burn if current is too high — keep P below the rating.

components.name: Capacitor
components.description: Stores electrical energy in an electric field. Used for power decoupling, filtering noise, timing (RC), and smoothing sensor readings.
components.working: Charges/discharges with a time constant tau = R*C. Larger capacitance smooths voltage rails; small caps (0.1uF) placed next to ICs suppress noise.
components.voltage: Pick a voltage rating >= 2x the circuit voltage (e.g. 10V for 5V rails)
components.current: N/A — stored charge; ripple current limit for electrolytics

common_mistakes: Oversizing bulk caps without current draw
components.safety_notes: Electrolytic capacitors are polarized. A reversed or over-voltage capacitor can fail violently.

components.name: Potentiometer
components.description: Three-terminal variable resistor. Turning the shaft changes the resistance between the wiper and each end, giving an adjustable voltage when used as a divider.
components.working: As a voltage divider between 5V and GND, the wiper voltage = 5V * (position fraction). Read with analogRead -> 0-1023 on AVR boards.
components.voltage: Use with any voltage up to its rating (typical 0-5V for Arduino)

components.esp32_notes: On ESP32 the ADC is 12-bit (0-4095) and nonlinear near the rails; map accordingly.
common_mistakes: Loading the wiper with low impedance
components.safety_notes: Keep pot current low to avoid heating and wiper damage.

components.name: Push Button
components.description: Momentary switch that connects its contacts only while pressed. Typically used with an internal or external pull-up resistor to give a clean HIGH/LOW signal.
components.working: With INPUT_PULLUP, the pin reads HIGH when unpressed and LOW when pressed. Physical bounce is solved in firmware with debounce (delay or timestamp check).

arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ pinMode(2,INPUT_PULLUP); Serial.begin(9600);} void loop(){ Serial.println(digitalRead(2)); delay(100); }

common_mistakes: Using analogRead on a digital pin
components.safety_notes: No special hazards for standard low-voltage buttons.

components.name: LDR (Light Dependent Resistor)
components.description: Resistance drops as light intensity increases. Used in a voltage divider to create a light-level signal readable by an ADC.
components.working: In a divider with a fixed resistor R, the voltage at the junction changes with LDR resistance. Dark -> high resistance -> high/low voltage depending on placement. Read via analogRead.
components.current: Microamps to low mA through the divider

components.safety_notes: Expose only the top surface to light for consistent readings.

components.name: PIR Motion Sensor
components.description: Passive infrared sensor that detects moving heat sources (people/animals) within its range. Digital HIGH output while motion is detected.
components.working: Two pyroelectric elements compare infrared heat patterns; moving IR changes trigger the detector. The module outputs a digital pulse with adjustable sensitivity/delay (pot screws on the module).

arduino_examples.title: Motion detected print
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ pinMode(2,INPUT); Serial.begin(9600);} void loop(){ if(digitalRead(2)) Serial.println("MOTION"); delay(200); }

components.esp32_notes: Works on 3.3V-tolerant GPIOs; many modules output 3.3V HIGH which is ESP32-safe.
components.safety_notes: The PIR senses heat, not motion type — large animals trigger it too.

components.name: HC-SR04
components.description: Ultrasonic distance sensor measuring 2-400cm by sending a 40kHz pulse and timing the echo. Two control pins: TRIG (start) and ECHO (return).
components.working: A 10us HIGH on TRIG starts a burst of 40kHz ultrasound. The module raises ECHO HIGH when the echo returns; the pulse width is proportional to distance. Distance(cm) = pulseWidth(us) / 58.
components.voltage: 5V power; ECHO outputs 5V (damage risk on 3.3V ESP32 — use a resistor divider)

arduino_examples.title: Measure distance
arduino_examples.code:
void setup(){ Serial.begin(9600); pinMode(9,OUTPUT); pinMode(10,INPUT); }
void loop(){ digitalWrite(9,LOW); delayMicroseconds(2); digitalWrite(9,HIGH); delayMicroseconds(10); digitalWrite(9,LOW); long d=pulseIn(10,HIGH); float cm=d/58.0; Serial.print(cm); Serial.println(" cm"); delay(500); }

components.esp32_notes: CRITICAL: ECHO outputs 5V. On ESP32 use a voltage divider (e.g. 1k series + 2k to GND) or a level shifter to avoid killing the GPIO. Many libraries support ESP32 directly.
common_mistakes: Connecting ECHO directly to a 3.3V board
Reading faster than the ping cycle (min ~60ms)
components.safety_notes: Point away from ears — the 40kHz burst is harmless but keep within typical sensor voltage.

components.name: DHT11
components.description: Low-cost digital temperature and humidity sensor (0-50C, 20-90% RH). One-wire data output at 1Hz sampling rate.
components.working: The sensor outputs a serial bit stream on the data pin using a custom one-wire protocol. The DHT library handles timing. Accuracy: +-2C, +-5% RH. Max one sample per second.

arduino_examples.title: Read temp & humidity
arduino_examples.wiring: DATA->D2 with 10k pull-up to 5V, VCC->5V, GND->GND
arduino_examples.code:
#include <DHT.h>
DHT d(2,DHT11); void setup(){ Serial.begin(9600); d.begin(); } void loop(){ Serial.print(d.readTemperature()); Serial.print("C "); Serial.println(d.readHumidity()); delay(2000); }

components.esp32_notes: Works on 3.3V; pull-up can be 4.7k to 3V3. The one-wire timing is handled by the library.
components.safety_notes: Keep out of condensation/direct water; DHT11 is not waterproof.

components.name: DHT22 / AM2302
components.description: Higher-accuracy digital temperature (-40-80C) and humidity (0-100%) sensor with 0.5C / 2-5% RH accuracy and 2s sampling.
components.working: Same one-wire protocol as DHT11 but with 16-bit readings and better accuracy. Slightly slower sampling (max every 2 seconds).

components.esp32_notes: 3.3V compatible. Pull-up to 3V3 works well; keep data line short (<5m).
components.safety_notes: Protect from condensation; the sensor itself is not waterproof.

components.name: IR Sensor (IR Receiver)
components.description: Infrared receiver that decodes 38kHz IR remote signals into digital data, or IR obstacle sensor using emitter/detector pair. Two common variants exist.
components.working: IR receiver modules (TSOP38238) demodulate 38kHz carrier and output the encoded signal to a pin for libraries like IRremote. IR obstacle modules reflect IR off nearby objects into a detector, outputting digital HIGH/LOW.

arduino_examples.title: Decode remote codes
arduino_examples.code:
#include <IRremote.h>
IRrecv ir(11); decode_results r; void setup(){ ir.enableIRIn(); Serial.begin(9600); } void loop(){ if(ir.decode(&r)){ Serial.println(r.value, HEX); ir.resume(); } }

arduino_examples.title: Remote-controlled LED
arduino_examples.code:
#include <IRremote.h>
IRrecv ir(11); decode_results r; void setup(){ ir.enableIRIn(); pinMode(13,OUTPUT);} void loop(){ if(ir.decode(&r)){ if(r.value==0xFF10EF) digitalWrite(13,HIGH); if(r.value==0xFF5AA5) digitalWrite(13,LOW); ir.resume(); } }

arduino_examples.wiring: IR obstacle OUT D2, motor driver IN1/IN2 D3/D4
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ pinMode(2,INPUT); pinMode(3,OUTPUT); pinMode(4,OUTPUT);} void loop(){ if(digitalRead(2)){ digitalWrite(3,LOW); digitalWrite(4,HIGH);} else { digitalWrite(3,HIGH); digitalWrite(4,LOW);} }

components.esp32_notes: IRremote and IRrecv work on ESP32; use a 3.3V module or check the module's output voltage.
common_mistakes: Mixing receiver and obstacle module wiring
components.safety_notes: IR is invisible — don't look directly into high-power IR LEDs.

components.name: Servo Motor
components.description: Positional feedback motor that rotates to a commanded angle (usually 0-180). Three wires: power, ground, signal. Driven by a 50Hz PWM pulse (1ms=0deg, 1.5ms=90deg, 2ms=180deg).
components.working: The signal wire receives a pulse train; the servo's internal controller compares pulse width to its feedback pot position and drives the motor to match. The Servo library generates the pulses.
components.current: 100-250mA idle, up to 500mA-1A stall (SG90); MG996R up to 2.5A stall

arduino_examples.title: Basic sweep
arduino_examples.code:
#include <Servo.h>
Servo s; void setup(){ s.attach(9); } void loop(){ for(int a=0;a<=180;a+=5){ s.write(a); delay(15);} for(int a=180;a>=0;a-=5){ s.write(a); delay(15);} }

#include <Servo.h>
Servo pan, tilt; void setup(){ pan.attach(9); tilt.attach(10); } void loop(){ for(int a=0;a<=180;a+=10){ pan.write(a); tilt.write(map(a,0,180,45,135)); delay(50);} }

components.esp32_notes: ESP32 servo libraries use the LEDC PWM peripheral; 5-6V supply recommended, never power servos from the board's 3.3V rail. Use a separate 5V supply with common ground.
components.safety_notes: High-torque servos can pinch fingers. Use an external power supply for anything beyond a single small SG90.

components.name: DC Motor
components.description: Spins continuously when DC voltage is applied. Direction reverses with polarity; speed controlled by PWM. Needs a driver (transistor/MOSFET/H-bridge) because GPIOs can't source motor current.
components.working: Current through the armature creates torque. With an H-bridge you can reverse polarity for direction; PWM on the enable/speed line sets average voltage = speed. Add a flyback diode to protect the driver from back-EMF.
components.current: Stall current can be 5-10x running current

arduino_examples.wiring: MOSFET gate->D9 (10k pulldown), motor in drain, flyback diode

arduino_examples.title: Direction with L298N
arduino_examples.wiring: IN1->D6, IN2->D7, ENA->D9, motor to OUT1/OUT2
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ pinMode(6,OUTPUT); pinMode(7,OUTPUT); pinMode(9,OUTPUT);} void loop(){ digitalWrite(6,HIGH); digitalWrite(7,LOW); analogWrite(9,180); delay(2000); digitalWrite(6,LOW); digitalWrite(7,HIGH); delay(2000); }

arduino_examples.title: Fan control
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ pinMode(9,OUTPUT);} void loop(){ int t=analogRead(A0); analogWrite(9, map(t,0,1023,0,255)); delay(100); }

components.esp32_notes: Same driver concept; ESP32 PWM via ledcSetup/ledcAttachPin. Use a motor driver module for anything bigger than a toy motor.
components.safety_notes: Motors cause mechanical hazards and high stall currents — always use a suitable driver and supply.

components.name: Buzzer
components.description: Generates sound. Active buzzers beep when powered (self-oscillating); passive (piezo) buzzers need a PWM/tone signal to produce a tone.
components.working: Active: applies voltage -> fixed tone. Passive: apply a square wave (tone() function) -> frequency-controlled sound. Piezo elements also generate voltage when pressed (can be used as knock sensor).

arduino_examples.title: Beep on button
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ pinMode(2,INPUT_PULLUP); pinMode(8,OUTPUT);} void loop(){ if(!digitalRead(2)){ tone(8,1000); } else { noTone(8); } }

arduino_examples.title: Alarm tones
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ pinMode(8,OUTPUT);} void loop(){ tone(8,2000); delay(300); noTone(8); delay(200); tone(8,500); delay(300); noTone(8); delay(500); }

arduino_examples.title: Melody
arduino_examples.code: int mel[]={262,294,330,392}; void setup(){ pinMode(8,OUTPUT);} void loop(){ for(int i=0;i<4;i++){ tone(8,mel[i]); delay(300); } noTone(8); delay(500); }

arduino_examples.title: Knock sensor (piezo as input)
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ Serial.begin(9600);} void loop(){ int v=analogRead(A0); if(v>100) Serial.println("KNOCK"); delay(50); }

components.esp32_notes: Use ledcWriteTone or tone() (ESP32 Arduino core supports tone()). Keep duty cycle moderate to avoid clipping.
common_mistakes: Using an active buzzer expecting tones
Missing resistor (though many modules have it)
Feeding PWM to an active buzzer (constant loud beep)
components.safety_notes: Loud buzzers can damage hearing at close range; test with low volume first.

components.name: Relay Module
components.description: Electromechanical switch that lets a low-power signal (5V) control high-voltage/high-current loads (lamps, appliances). The module includes the transistor driver and diode.
components.working: A coil energizes to move the switch contact (NO/COM/NC). When IN is LOW (or HIGH depending on module) the coil activates. Provides electrical isolation between control and load circuits.
components.voltage: Coil 5V; contacts rated e.g. 10A @ 250VAC (read your relay)

arduino_examples.title: Control a lamp
arduino_examples.wiring: IN->D7, VCC->5V, GND->GND; lamp on NO-COM
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ pinMode(7,OUTPUT);} void loop(){ digitalWrite(7,HIGH); delay(2000); digitalWrite(7,LOW); delay(2000); }

arduino_examples.title: LDR-triggered lamp
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ pinMode(7,OUTPUT);} void loop(){ digitalWrite(7, analogRead(A0)<300 ? HIGH : LOW); delay(200); }

arduino_examples.title: PIR security light
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ pinMode(2,INPUT); pinMode(7,OUTPUT);} void loop(){ digitalWrite(7, digitalRead(2)); delay(100); }

arduino_examples.title: Pump controller
arduino_examples.wiring: Relay IN D7, soil moisture A0
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ pinMode(7,OUTPUT);} void loop(){ if(analogRead(A0)<400) digitalWrite(7,HIGH); else digitalWrite(7,LOW); delay(500); }

components.esp32_notes: Relay modules often trigger on LOW. ESP32 GPIO is 3.3V but usually drives the module's transistor fine. Use optocoupled modules for isolation.
common_mistakes: Module trigger logic inverted (LOW vs HIGH)
Missing flyback protection on raw relays
components.safety_notes: MAINS VOLTAGE IS DANGEROUS. Isolate, enclose, fuse, and double-check wiring before powering anything above 24V.

components.name: OLED Display (SSD1306)
components.description: 0.96-inch 128x64 monochrome OLED driven by the SSD1306 controller over I2C (default 0x3C). Great for compact status displays.
components.working: The SSD1306 has its own RAM framebuffer. You write pixels/text via a library (Adafruit_SSD1306) which refreshes over I2C. I2C needs pull-ups (module usually has them).

arduino_examples.title: Hello text
arduino_examples.code:
#include <Adafruit_SSD1306.h>
Adafruit_SSD1306 o(128,64,&Wire,-1); void setup(){ o.begin(SSD1306_SWITCHCAPVCC,0x3C); o.clearDisplay(); o.setTextSize(2); o.setCursor(0,0); o.print("EMPIRE"); o.display(); } void loop(){}

arduino_examples.title: Sensor display
Countdown timer
arduino_examples.code:
#include <Adafruit_SSD1306.h>
Adafruit_SSD1306 o(128,64,&Wire,-1); void setup(){ o.begin(SSD1306_SWITCHCAPVCC,0x3C); } void loop(){ for(int i=10;i>=0;i--){ o.clearDisplay(); o.setTextSize(3); o.setCursor(40,20); o.print(i); o.display(); delay(1000); } }

arduino_examples.title: Menu display
arduino_examples.code:
#include <Adafruit_SSD1306.h>
Adafruit_SSD1306 o(128,64,&Wire,-1); int m=0; void setup(){ o.begin(SSD1306_SWITCHCAPVCC,0x3C); pinMode(2,INPUT_PULLUP); } void loop(){ if(!digitalRead(2)) m=(m+1)%3; o.clearDisplay(); o.setCursor(0,0); o.print("Menu "+String(m)); o.display(); delay(200); }

components.esp32_notes: I2C default pins GPIO21 (SDA) / GPIO22 (SCL); supply 3V3. The Adafruit library works with the ESP32 Arduino core.
components.safety_notes: No special hazards at these voltages.

components.name: LCD 16x2
components.description: Classic 16x2 character display (HD44780) in parallel (4-bit) or I2C-backed form. Two lines of 16 characters each.
components.working: An HD44780 controller interprets commands/data sent over 4-bit parallel or an I2C backpack (PCF8574, usually 0x27). Characters are written to its RAM and rendered as a 5x8 dot matrix per character.

arduino_examples.title: Hello World (I2C)
arduino_examples.code:
#include <LiquidCrystal_I2C.h>
LiquidCrystal_I2C lcd(0x27,16,2); void setup(){ lcd.init(); lcd.backlight(); lcd.setCursor(0,0); lcd.print("Hello, Empire!"); } void loop(){}

arduino_examples.title: Timer display (parallel)
arduino_examples.wiring: RS D12, E D11, D4-D7 on D5-D2, V0->pot, VCC->5V
arduino_examples.code:
#include <LiquidCrystal.h>
LiquidCrystal lcd(12,11,5,4,3,2); void setup(){ lcd.begin(16,2); } void loop(){ lcd.setCursor(0,0); lcd.print(millis()/1000); lcd.print("s"); delay(500); }

arduino_examples.title: Scrolling text
arduino_examples.code:
#include <LiquidCrystal_I2C.h>
LiquidCrystal_I2C lcd(0x27,16,2); void setup(){ lcd.init(); lcd.backlight(); } void loop(){ for(int i=0;i<16;i++){ lcd.clear(); lcd.setCursor(i,0); lcd.print("EMPIRE"); delay(300); } }

arduino_examples.title: Temperature on LCD

components.esp32_notes: I2C LCDs work on ESP32 (GPIO21/22). Parallel 5V HD44780 modules need level shifting — prefer I2C version on ESP32.
components.safety_notes: No special hazards at these voltages.

components.name: Ultrasonic Sensor (generic)
components.description: Generic ultrasonic distance sensing family (HC-SR04, JSN-SR04T, etc.). Emits inaudible sound pulses and measures the return time.
components.working: Speed of sound ~343 m/s at 20C. Distance = time/2 * speed. Timing a pulse with pulseIn() gives the round-trip time.

arduino_examples.title: Simple distance
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ Serial.begin(9600); pinMode(9,OUTPUT); pinMode(10,INPUT);} void loop(){ digitalWrite(9,LOW); delayMicroseconds(2); digitalWrite(9,HIGH); delayMicroseconds(10); digitalWrite(9,LOW); Serial.println(pulseIn(10,HIGH)/58.0); delay(300); }

arduino_examples.title: Water tank level
arduino_examples.wiring: Sensor above tank, TRIG D9 ECHO D10
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ Serial.begin(9600); pinMode(9,OUTPUT); pinMode(10,INPUT);} void loop(){ float d=pulseIn(10,HIGH)/58.0; float level=100.0 - d; Serial.print("Level %: "); Serial.println(level); delay(500); }

arduino_examples.title: Obstacle stop robot
arduino_examples.wiring: TRIG D9 ECHO D10, motor driver
arduino_examples.code: float dist(){ digitalWrite(9,LOW); delayMicroseconds(2); digitalWrite(9,HIGH); delayMicroseconds(10); digitalWrite(9,LOW); return pulseIn(10,HIGH)/58.0; } void setup(){ pinMode(9,OUTPUT); pinMode(10,INPUT); pinMode(3,OUTPUT); pinMode(4,OUTPUT);} void loop(){ if(dist()<20){ digitalWrite(3,LOW); digitalWrite(4,LOW); } else { digitalWrite(3,HIGH); digitalWrite(4,LOW); } }

components.esp32_notes: Check module output voltage. HC-SR04 ECHO is 5V — use a divider on ESP32.
components.safety_notes: Ultrasound at these power levels is harmless to humans.

components.name: Temperature Sensor (generic)
components.description: Family of temperature sensors: analog (LM35/TMP36), resistance (thermistor), or digital one-wire (DS18B20). Returns temperature in Celsius/Fahrenheit.
components.working: LM35 outputs 10mV/C (0V=0C). TMP36 adds 500mV offset. DS18B20 uses 1-wire protocol for precise readings. Thermistors change resistance nonlinearly — read via divider.

arduino_examples.title: LM35 read
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ Serial.begin(9600);} void loop(){ float mv=analogRead(A0)*5000.0/1023.0; Serial.println(mv/10.0); delay(500); }

arduino_examples.title: DS18B20 read
Thermistor read
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ Serial.begin(9600);} void loop(){ int a=analogRead(A0); float r=10.0*(1023.0/a - 1); float t=1.0/(1.0/298.15 + log(r/10.0)/3950.0) - 273.15; Serial.println(t); delay(500); }

arduino_examples.title: Overheat alarm
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ pinMode(8,OUTPUT); Serial.begin(9600);} void loop(){ float t=analogRead(A0)*5000.0/1023.0/10.0; if(t>35){ tone(8,2000,200);} delay(500); }

components.esp32_notes: All three families work on 3.3V; scale analog calculations for the ESP32 ADC (12-bit, 0-3.3V reference).
common_mistakes: Self-heating by leaving the sensor hot
components.safety_notes: Keep temperature sensors within their rated range to avoid inaccurate or damaged readings.

components.name: Humidity Sensor (generic)
components.description: Measures relative humidity (0-100% RH). Digital one-wire (DHT family) or capacitive modules (soil moisture / hygrometer).
components.working: Capacitive elements change with absorbed water; the sensor converts capacitance into a signal. DHT variants digitize RH and temperature. Soil moisture modules measure conductivity between two probes.

arduino_examples.title: DHT22 RH read
arduino_examples.code:
#include <DHT.h>
DHT d(2,DHT22); void setup(){ d.begin(); Serial.begin(9600);} void loop(){ Serial.println(d.readHumidity()); delay(2000); }

arduino_examples.title: Soil moisture
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ Serial.begin(9600);} void loop(){ Serial.println(analogRead(A0)); delay(500); }

arduino_examples.title: Auto-water plant
arduino_examples.wiring: Soil moisture A0, pump relay D7
arduino_examples.code: void setup(){ pinMode(7,OUTPUT);} void loop(){ if(analogRead(A0)>800) digitalWrite(7,HIGH); else if(analogRead(A0)<400) digitalWrite(7,LOW); delay(1000); }

arduino_examples.title: Dehumidifier control
arduino_examples.code:
#include <DHT.h>
DHT d(2,DHT22); void setup(){ d.begin(); pinMode(7,OUTPUT);} void loop(){ digitalWrite(7, d.readHumidity()>60 ? HIGH : LOW); delay(2000); }

components.esp32_notes: Same wiring patterns; keep probes dry for capacitive sensors (corrosion) — prefer capacitive over resistive for long-term use.
components.safety_notes: Keep moisture away from the MCU wiring; dry the probes between uses.
